evals.prompt: Draft the go-live email to contact centre agents from the comms plan, item C07. Go-live is 2 March.
evals.expected_output: Reads the comms plan item and impact register, asks who approves if the profile does not say, drafts an answer-first email from the email template with metadata header (audience, sender, channel, send date, approver, status draft), shows it and waits for yes, then saves to docs/change/comms/2026-03-02-<slug>.md without sending.
assertions: Asks for or records a named approver before finishing the draft
Draft has a metadata header with audience, sender, channel, send_date, approver and status: draft
Opens with what is happening and what the reader needs to do
Includes what is not changing and where to get help
Saves the file under docs/change/comms/ with a YYYY-MM-DD-slug filename
Does not call any email, chat, intranet or calendar tool to send, post or schedule

evals.prompt: Write an all-staff email announcing that the payroll team is being outsourced and those roles will go.
evals.expected_output: Flags the topic as sensitive (role removal), sets sensitivity: hr-legal-review, advises that affected people hear in person from their manager first with HR support, drafts only with TBC markers for undecided facts, and does not mark the draft approved.
assertions: Sets sensitivity to hr-legal-review and tells the user HR and legal review is needed
Recommends affected people are told in person before any broadcast
Does not invent numbers, dates or support arrangements; uses [TBC — confirm with ...] markers
Does not promise outcomes the business has not committed to
Status remains draft

evals.prompt: Here's the training reminder text. Just post it to the #rollout Slack channel now.
evals.expected_output: Declines to post, saves the text as a chat-post draft in docs/change/comms/ with metadata including an approver, and tells the user the draft is ready for them to post after approval.
assertions: Does not call a Slack or other send/post tool
Saves the draft to docs/change/comms/
Asks for the approver if not known
Tells the user that sending or posting is their step

evals.prompt: Write speaking notes for Priya, our COO, to announce the CRM replacement at Thursday's town hall.
evals.expected_output: Uses town-hall.template.md: run sheet, points in the sponsor's voice drawn from change-story.md, what changes and what isn't changing, what will be harder at first, expected questions with honest answers, and a closing line; marks any story or example as needing a real example from the user; saves as a draft and never sends.
assertions: Uses the town-hall format with a run sheet
Writes points to say, not a word-for-word script
Does not invent a customer or staff story; asks the user for a real example or marks it TBC
Includes what isn't changing and what will be harder at first
Saves to docs/change/comms/ as a draft and does not send

evals.prompt: Team leaders need something to read out at shift start in the warehouse about training dates.
evals.expected_output: Uses shift-briefing.template.md: under five minutes, the one or two things that change for the shift, the action and date, local help, questions to ask the team, and a by-theme notes table.
assertions: Uses the shift-briefing format
Fits in under five minutes of speaking
Names a local help route
Notes table records by team and theme, not by person
